Represent transitions between latent states as a network

Source: R/tna.R
get_tna.Rd

get_tna() constructs a network summarising transitions between latent profiles or classes across ordered observations. The profiles or classes form the nodes, and directed edge weights represent transition probabilities, including the probability of remaining in the same state. The returned network supports visualisation and analysis with the tna package.

For a supported latent transition model, the network uses model-estimated transitions, pooling expected transitions across latent group classes. For a profile or class model fitted with time, it instead summarises transitions between the most probable class assignments in each group's ordered sequence.

Usage

get_tna(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A time-homogeneous fitted model from lta(), or a multilpa() or multilca() model fitted with time, for which the network is based on modal profile sequences.

...

Passed to tna::tna().

Value

An object of class tna, as returned by tna::tna(), to which the functions of the tna package apply, including centralities(), communities(), cliques() and plot().

Details

For a supported latent transition model, transition probabilities are the expected transition counts summed across group classes and normalised by row, so each class contributes in proportion to its share of the expected transitions, not its class probability. If a profile has no expected outgoing transitions in any class, its row is the class rows averaged by class probability, and a warning states that the row is unestimated; absent transitions are not treated as self-transitions.

For a multilpa() or multilca() fit, tna::tna() builds the network from the modal sequences. A fit made without time is refused.

A general lta() fit (occasion-varying or covariate-dependent transitions, second order, movers and stayers, or ordinal, count or weighted data) is currently unsupported and raises latents_unsupported_tna; its transitions are returned by get_results(x, "transitions").

Interpretation

A network built from modal assignments is a descriptive summary and does not account for classification uncertainty. A pooled network may conceal differences between latent group classes; use get_group_tna() to examine their separate networks.

See also

get_group_tna() for one network per latent group class.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("tna", quietly = TRUE)) {
  activity <- c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read")
  moves <- lta(course_engagement, vars = activity, id = "student",
                           time = "sequence", n_profiles = 2,
                           n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
  get_tna(moves)
}
#> State Labels : 
#> 
#>    profile_1, profile_2 
#> 
#> Transition Probability Matrix :
#> 
#>           profile_1 profile_2
#> profile_1 0.8626339 0.1373661
#> profile_2 0.1848036 0.8151964
#> 
#> Initial Probabilities : 
#> 
#> profile_1 profile_2 
#> 0.6324903 0.3675097
